items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: Now when I first went away with Basie, that was the most money I made with a big band.

ctx.x: Yeah. What kind of, we talked about how you changed band to band, you got better pay. What kind of pay were you getting in those days? What was a good salary in those days?

Well, I'm ashamed to say it, but at that time the money wasn't like it is now. When I first went away with Lionel Hampton, I was making nineteen dollars a night. Now that nineteen dollars, if you just work one week, I mean one night, you just got nineteen dollars. Then, after I left, I started, when I came back, I was making about twenty-five. For a night? Yeah. For a night, yeah. Yeah. Now when I first went away with Basie, that was the most money I made with a big band. I was getting three hundred dollars a…
Now who paid the hotel? We had to pay the hotel.

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: Like when I was playing with Carl Basie. He had a hit arrangement on.

ctx.x: Did you feel comfortable with them? Yes.

You know, I hated to leave those guys. I hated to leave those guys. I hated to leave those guys. I hated to leave those guys. I hated them so many years. I do it my way. You do it your way. And it doesn't go that way. If they were playing with any major band, you have to play the way you want. The arrangement called. Like when I was playing with Carl Basie. He had a hit arrangement on. I mean a hit record on. I said, I can't stop loving you. I played with Ray Charles for two years before that. He had also had a…
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I suppose you had a first base when you said, well you guys play baseball. You're well played my way. But what happened to the team? It's the same thing to me.
